source.title: When Forgetting Builds Reliability: LLM Unlearning for Reliable Hardware Code Generation
source.authors: Yiwen Liang; Qiufeng Li; Shikai Wang; Weidong Cao

record.tranche_reason: Applies unlearning methods and measures forgetting and retained utility in RTL code generation, a domain-specific setting. It does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: Reports PrivLeak, MinK++, and utility after unlearning, but no fine-tuning recovery attack, activation ablation or analysis, quantization, or prompt-based recovery. The paper's discussion of other unlearning studies is not recorded as results. Rows record Table II MinK++ for GA, SimNPO, and the proposed method, plus Pass@1 for the proposed method; the paper also reports other metrics not included here.
record.test_reason: An unlearning-method paper for RTL code generation. It reports only its own method against GA and SimNPO on forgetting proxies (MinK++, PrivLeak) and utility. Unlearning runs 'until MinK++ converges near 0.5', so the forgetting score is a stopping criterion, not an outcome. No recovery attack of any kind (fine-tuning, ablation, quantization, prompting) is run, and targeted-knowledge accuracy is never measured. Its results therefore do not bear on whether unlearning is shallow or robust.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that syntax-preserving masking plus FiFSL gives near-complete forgetting, typically in one epoch, while preserving syntactic and functional RTL utility. They also claim it supports forget sets up to 3× larger than GA/SimNPO; for Llama-3-8B the limit is 20%.
record.recipe_differences: The proposed method adds syntax-preserving masking and FiFSL; GA and SimNPO are used as unlearning baselines. The study does not reproduce recovery attacks from the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Forget-set size and model affect the reported forgetting and utility results; the paper notes Llama-3-8B supports only up to 20% forgetting, unlike the coder models.

fits_no_version.finding: In RTL code LLMs, GA and SimNPO reach MinK++ about 0.5 but lose much Pass@1 at 20–30% forget sets (e.g. Llama-7B 30%: 3%/1%). The syntax-masked FiFSL method keeps Pass@1 within about 5 points, except Llama-8B at 30% (24%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Domain-specific (syntax-preserving) unlearning reduces utility collateral relative to GA/SimNPO in code generation, measured with membership-proxy forgetting metrics.

record.problems: Forget sets are subsamples of the RTLCoder training corpus used to emulate problematic data, rather than reported proprietary or contaminated RTL examples. MinK++ and PrivLeak are forgetting proxies; no recovery attacks are run. No uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table II's PrivLeak, loss, BLEU, and chrF results and Table III benchmark results are omitted; the recorded measures prioritize forgetting proxy and retained Pass@1 utility. No rows are omitted due to the row cap.

untested.parts: Targeted-knowledge accuracy is not measured; forgetting is a membership proxy used as a stopping criterion; no attack tests whether knowledge is recoverable.
No activation ablation or access-vs-deletion analysis.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, cross-lingual or in-context recovery.
The proposed method is not claimed or tested to resist recovery attacks.

record.verdict_notes: Row fixes are grouped by range (r01-r36, r37-r48) because every row needs the same correction. No verdict labels are given: the study does not test any version, and its MinK++ values are set by the stopping rule. The reader's 'tests'/T3 classification and its 'supports' label for A should be dropped.

versions.untested_parts: Tests forgetting quality using PrivLeak and MinK++ and retained utility using Pass@1; does not test whether simple attacks recover the knowledge, or targeted-knowledge accuracy directly.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning attack.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis of access versus deletion.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context recovery test.
The proposed method is not evaluated for resistance to the attacks in the claim.
